title: Connected browser telemetry and warm native cache scaling

training_method.label: Frozen-base QKV LoRA
training_method.description: Complete summed FP32 gradients for rank-4 QKV adapters with one canonical coordinator AdamW update.

execution_topology.label: Authenticated two-assignment data parallel
execution_topology.description: Two disjoint checkpoint-bound assignments execute independently and aggregate once at the coordinator.

memory_profiles.label: Browser WASM resident
memory_profiles.description: Burn NdArray CPU/WASM with the fetched base and adapter resident in the browser runtime.

memory_profiles.label: Native cached FP32 resident
memory_profiles.description: Digest-validated safetensors persist on local storage; each one-shot native process loads the complete FP32 base into system RAM.

numerical_profiles.label: FP32 summed adapter gradients
numerical_profiles.description: Workers return every declared adapter tensor before coordinator normalization and clipping.

worker_profiles.label: Burn CPU/WASM browser
worker_profiles.description: Headless Chromium 150 running Burn 0.21 NdArray through WASM.

worker_profiles.label: Native Python/PyTorch CPU
worker_profiles.description: One-shot isolated native processes using the authenticated worker CLI and a shared content-addressed disk cache.

reproduction.notes: The automated script reproduces the T1 and T2 native profiles with isolated worker processes and deletes ephemeral worker-token files. The connected browser measurement additionally requires two local authenticated CPU/WASM page runs; payload byte counts describe worker API response bodies and do not distinguish browser HTTP-cache hits or packet-level wire bytes.
